execution.description: Native synthetic/public control regressions and three-item P1/P2/A4 registration checks; no host, solver or protected input execution.

expected: A live checker must accept a positive witness and refuse its known-bad control for the specific reason. Missing controls and missing numerical noise must not become controlled readiness.
observed: 156 final native tests passed, 12 Linux-dependent tests deselected; baseline failures from absent temporary parent and Windows fcntl were preserved as diagnostic failures, not science failures. The canonical wrapper refused Windows-managed worktree identity; pinned CI remains required. Public subset controlled PASS counts are battery 3/3, motor 2/3, cooling 2/3; the latter two retain pending operator identity and all partial runs remain unready. Always-pass, always-fail, wrong-reason, malformed-result and raising fixtures earn no controlled pass. Synthetic noise changes alter the controlled count without a qualification claim. Finite-extreme quantile, both CLI routing signs and deliberately mutating checker context isolation have explicit controls. The owner resolved the delivery/Hub hold; canonical checks and domain/host constraints remain.
keep: Original roster, values, reviews, waivers and historical report interpretation.
change: Report control/specimen/code identities and both signs beside original status; require controlled_ready for CLI success.
review_repair: PKT14-R1/R2 reproduced as two failing native regressions on the reviewed code. Fresh per-sign evidence_paths now prevent a stateful checker faking detection via a shared marker, and specimen_digest binds the pre-invocation known-bad input. The focused post-repair control module passed 52 tests; the earlier 156-test native diagnostic suite was not duplicated. New-head canonical acceptance remains required. Neither reproduction is evidence of a production leak or a changed physical passing count.
